 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. On Wednesday, the Los Angeles Lakers and the Golden State Warriors faced off in their 2026-27 NBA season opener in LA. Energy and intensity flooded Crypto.com Arena on and off the court as players and fans relished the moment. But for Golden State rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, his NBA debut didn't go the way he wanted.
 With Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody out injured, Lendeborg got the start at wing, and he faced off against two-time NBA scoring champion Luka Dončić for most of the game. He held his own, holding Dončić to 1-of-6 shooting as the primary defender, according to Anthony Slater of ESPN. Throughout the game, both players were seen jawing at each other, and Lendeborg was ultimately given a technical foul. The Lakers defeated the Warriors 127-105, and the rookie had a lot to say in a postgame interview about Dončić's on-court antics.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I had a lot of respect for him [because] I didn't really watch the NBA much," Lendeborg said, via ESPN . "I just watched highlights and seen him kill people. But being in it firsthand and seeing all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect."
 Lendeborg admitted that he was "telling him he sucks" during one of their exchanges. But Dončić got the last laugh at the end of the first half, banking in a 48-foot heave at the buzzer and then pointing and laughing at Lendeborg.
 Warriors head coach Steve Kerr thought the officials got it wrong.
 "I thought the single technical was ridiculous. They were jawing at each other," Kerr said. "I think it was the words Yaxel used that got him the T. But then Luka makes the half-court shot and gets in his face. That should be a tech."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Dončić, meanwhile, said he tried to stay out of it.
 "He was talking crazy," Dončić said. "But I wasn't trying to talk back. This season, I'm not trying to get techs."
 ESPN analyst Stephen A. Smith applauded Lendeborg for his brazen comments and agreed players needed to stop whining to the officials on a recent episode of First Take .
 "Here's why I'm supportive of what Yaxel is saying," Smith said. "He's saying 'if you're so great, quit whining to the officials. Just go out there and bust my ass. But stop whining to the officials, looking to them for help.' I was really ticked off when that ref gave Yaxel that technical… I'm calling out the NBA. NBA, gotta stop that nonsense! Let them talk!"
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Lendeborg was obviously frustrated by his first experience in the NBA, as Dončić has a habit of frustrating defenses.
 "I guess this is what the NBA is like, man," Lendeborg said. "A lot of flopping, a lot of foul baiting, a lot of praying to the refs, man. Interesting first game for me."
 It will be interesting to see the direction the NBA takes with their officiating teams this year, as the NFL currently faces backlash for theirs.
